candidates.label: Malta (island)
candidates.support: The overwhelming majority of scholars, following continuous local tradition, ancient geographic usage of the name 'Melite,' and the sailing route described in Acts 27, identify the 'Melita' of Acts 28:1 with the island of Malta, south of Sicily; Pleiades and Wikidata's coordinates for the island agree closely.

candidates.label: Mljet (Melite Illyrica), Croatia
candidates.support: A minority proposal, argued most fully by the Ragusan scholar Ignjat Đurđević in the 1730s, holds that Paul's 'Melite' was instead the Adriatic island of Mljet (then called 'Melite Illyrica'), reasoning that the 'Adria' of Acts 27:27 points further north than Malta and that the island preserved its own tradition of Paul's shipwreck from at least the 10th century; this view has not displaced the mainstream identification with Malta.

summary.text: Malta is the Mediterranean island south of Sicily identified by mainstream scholarship as the 'Melita' where Paul was shipwrecked on his voyage to Rome; a minority view instead points to the Adriatic island of Mljet off the coast of Croatia. Acts recounts that the islanders showed Paul and his companions 'uncommon kindness,' that Paul was bitten by a viper without harm, and that he healed the father of Publius, the chief man of the island, along with other sick residents before the party's onward journey to Rome.

scripture.textWEB: When we had escaped, then they learned that the island was called Malta.
The natives showed us uncommon kindness; for they kindled a fire and received us all, because of the present rain and because of the cold.
Now in the neighborhood of that place were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius, who received us and courteously entertained us for three days.
Then when this was done, the rest also who had diseases in the island came and were cured.
